verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_jump_analyzer_test_video: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Single-letter names in the core detection logic: `m`, `g`, `n, lab, stats, cent`, `b`, `i`, `k_open`. `prep` is a vague name. Some constants have no rationale (`DIFF_THRESH = 30`, `MIN_AREA = 800`). The ground and apex logic is commented reasonably well.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Split into sensible functions (`read_frames`, `prep`, `athlete_boxes`, `analyze`, `main`), all short. But magic numbers are inline (`cross - 20`, `abs(i - cross) <= 8`, area `>= 40`, `percentile 99.5`), 960x540 is hardcoded in `prep`, and every frame is loaded into memory.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No `cap.isOpened()` check. An unreadable video gives empty frames, then `return 0, 0`, which is written as if it were a real result. With no detections it returns `0, len(frames)-1`, a fake result. No exit codes, and many inline magic constants.

items.name: Robust to bad inputs and missing detections
items.name_zh: 异常输入与检测失败的处理
items.evidence: Never checks that the video opened. When it fails it silently writes placeholders (`return 0, 0` / `return 0, len(frames) - 1`) with exit code 0. All thresholds are absolute pixel values tuned to the example (`HURDLE_X = 490`, `DIFF_THRESH = 30`, `AIR_MARGIN = 8`).

items.name: Output contract honoured
items.evidence: Reads input from `sys.argv[1]` and writes to `/app/output.toml` by default. Output has exactly two int fields with the correct names, via toml or an equivalent handwritten fallback. The 0-based frame numbering is stated in the final message.
